items.title: Trump to press Xi on Iran at Beijing summit this week

featured_image.name: Iran war adds tension to Trump-Xi summit in China

items.description: President Donald Trump will use his trip to China this week to pressure Chinese President Xi Jinping over Beijing's support for Iran, including its purchase of Iranian oil, sales of dual-use goods, and potential weapons exports to Tehran, a senior White House official said Sunday.[1][2]

items.title: Japan pushes for New Zealand to choose Mogami-class frigates over UK rival

featured_image.name: Japan, UK Compete to Supply Warships for New Zealand Navy Upgrade -  Bloomberg

items.description:
New Zealand has shortlisted Japan's upgraded Mogami-class frigate and Britain's Type 31 as the two contenders to replace its aging warships, setting the stage for a closely watched competition between Tokyo and London that carries broad implications for Indo-Pacific defense ties.

Defence Minister Chris Penk confirmed on May 7 that New Zealand has entered formal discussions with Australia and the United Kingdom on the frigate replacement, with a recommendation expected to reach the government by the end of 2027. The two Anzac-class frigates under consideration for replacement — HMNZS Te Kaha and HMNZS Te Mana — were commissioned in 1997 and 1999, respectively, and most of the navy's fleet is projected to reach the end of its design life by the mid-2030s.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran says 35 million people face water shortages as crises mount

featured_image.name: Iran faces unprecedented drought as water crisis hits Tehran

items.description: Iranian authorities warned on Monday that approximately 35 million people face water shortages heading into summer, as a convergence of drought, a U.S. naval blockade, mass layoffs, and a prolonged internet blackout pushes the country toward what analysts describe as a deepening domestic crisis.

items.title: Knesset passes law creating military tribunal for Oct. 7 suspects

featured_image.name: 'A modern Eichmann trial': Lawmakers, justice minister tout ...

items.description:
Israel's Knesset on Monday voted overwhelmingly to establish a special military tribunal to prosecute Palestinians detained during and after the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks, creating a legal framework that could lead to death sentences for those convicted of genocide and other charges.

The legislation, which passed its second and third readings with broad bipartisan support, establishes a dedicated military court in Jerusalem to try an estimated 350 to 400 suspects captured inside Israel between October 7 and October 10, 2023. The bill was co-sponsored by Religious Zionism MK Simcha Rothman and opposition lawmaker Yulia Malinovsky of Yisrael Beytenu.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Pakistan let Iran park warplanes on its airfields

featured_image.name: Iran submits response to latest US ceasefire proposal via ...

items.description:
Pakistan quietly allowed Iranian military aircraft to park at its airfields during the US-Iran conflict, even as Islamabad positioned itself as the central diplomatic broker between Washington and Tehran, CBS News reported on Monday, citing US officials with knowledge of the matter.[1]

The revelation complicates the image Pakistan has cultivated as a neutral intermediary in a war now in its tenth week, raising questions about how Islamabad balanced competing loyalties during one of the most volatile periods in the broader Middle East conflict.

items.title: EU set to sanction violent Israeli settlers after Hungary lifts veto

featured_image.name: Kaja Kallas, The EU's new Foreign Affairs Chief

items.description:
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Monday she expects a political agreement on sanctions targeting violent Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank, a measure that had been blocked for months by Hungary under former prime minister Viktor Orban.[1][2]

"I expect political agreement on the sanctions on violent settlers, hopefully we will get there," Kallas said ahead of a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Brussels, though she cautioned it was "still not entirely clear the required majority would be found".[3][2]

items.title: MSF suspends operations in Haiti's Cité Soleil as gang clashes force hospital evacuations

featured_image.name: Hospitals evacuated, MSF services halted as rival gangs clash in Haiti's  capital | Reuters

items.description: Hospitals in the Cité Soleil neighborhood of Haiti's capital, Port-au-Prince, evacuated their patients on Monday as Doctors Without Borders suspended all operations in the area amid escalating clashes between rival armed groups, according to Reuters. The violence, which intensified over the weekend, has left the densely populated district — home to hundreds of thousands — without a single functioning hospital.[1][2]

items.title: IDF sentences soldiers for desecrating Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon

featured_image.name: Photo shows Israeli soldier desecrating Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon

items.description:
The Israeli military on Monday sentenced two soldiers to military prison after one was photographed placing a cigarette in the mouth of a statue of the Virgin Mary in the southern Lebanese village of Debel, the second act of desecration against Christian symbols in the same village in recent weeks.

The soldier seen in the photograph received 21 days in military jail, while the soldier who took the photo was sentenced to 14 days, the IDF said. The sentencing was carried out by Brig. Gen. Sagiv Dahan, commander of the 162nd Division, who oversaw the relevant area of southern Lebanon at the time, according to the Times of Israel.[1][2]

items.title: EU's Kallas says Putin is 'weaker than ever' on Ukraine

featured_image.name: BELGIUM-EU-UKRAINE-CANADA-DIPLOMACY

items.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told reporters on Monday that Russian President Vladimir Putin is "in a weaker position than he has ever been before," following a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Brussels where the bloc adopted new sanctions over Russia's forced deportation of Ukrainian children and advanced plans for a more active European role in potential peace talks.

items.title: Trump says he'll raise Taiwan arms sales with Xi in Beijing

featured_image.name: When Trump meets Xi, Beijing will be 'working backward from our midterm  elections' | Fortune

items.description:
President Donald Trump said Monday he will bring up U.S. arms sales to Taiwan during his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing later this week, acknowledging China's opposition while declining to commit to continued weapons deliveries to the self-governing island.

"I'm going to have that discussion with President Xi," Trump told reporters at the White House. "President Xi would like us not to, and I'll have that discussion. That's one of the many things I'll be talking about."[1][2]

The remarks came as Trump prepares to depart for a two-day state visit to China scheduled for May 14–15, the first by a U.S. president in nearly nine years. The summit agenda spans trade, rare earth export controls, the war in Iran, artificial intelligence, and Taiwan.[3][4][5][6]

items.title: UAE secretly struck Iran's Lavan Island refinery, WSJ reports

featured_image.name: Unknown Enemy Attack Hits Lavan Island Refinery as Iran Assesses Damage —  UNITED24 Media

items.description: The United Arab Emirates carried out covert military strikes against Iran during the wider U.S.-Israeli war, including an attack on the oil refinery on Iran's Lavan Island on April 8 that triggered a large fire, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday. The revelation confirms weeks of speculation that the Gulf monarchy moved beyond its defensive posture to become a direct, if undeclared, participant in the conflict — a development that Washington quietly welcomed, according to Ynet News.[1][2]

items.title: Over 60 Labour MPs call on Starmer to resign as government aides quit

featured_image.name: Starmer 'gone by May' unless he changes course, Labour MPs warn

items.description: The rebellion against Prime Minister Keir Starmer escalated sharply on Monday as more than 60 Labour MPs publicly called on him to step down, and four junior members of the government resigned their posts to join the revolt. The growing mutiny, which now spans both the party's left and right flanks, represents the most serious internal threat to a sitting British prime minister in a generation.[1][2]

items.title: Trump says he may revive Strait of Hormuz operation

featured_image.name: Trump says US will start 'Project Freedom Plus' if Iran talks ...

items.description:
President Trump said Monday he is considering reviving "Project Freedom," the short-lived U.S. naval escort operation through the Strait of Hormuz, but warned that any renewed effort would go far beyond merely guiding ships and would be "only a piece" of a larger military operation.[1][2]

The remarks, made in a conversation with Fox News correspondent John Roberts, came after Trump on Sunday rejected Iran's counterproposal to end the roughly ten-week war as "totally unacceptable," posting on Truth Social: "I have just reviewed the reply from Iran's so-called 'Representatives.' I am not pleased — TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!"[3]

items.title: Iran releases Nobel laureate Mohammadi on bail amid health crisis

featured_image.name: Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi 'hospitalised' in Iran

items.description:
Iranian authorities released Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi on bail on Sunday and transferred her to a Tehran hospital for specialized medical treatment, her foundation announced, following weeks of mounting alarm over her deteriorating health in prison.[1][2][3]

The 54-year-old human rights activist had been held at Zanjan prison in northwestern Iran since her arrest on December 12, and her supporters said the transfer came after persistent appeals from her family, legal team, and international figures including the chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee.[4][1]

items.title: Trump says Iran cease-fire on 'massive life support'

featured_image.name: Trump doubles down on Iran threat, says ceasefire 'not good enough'

items.description:
President Trump on Monday cast doubt on the survival of the U.S.-Iran cease-fire, saying the agreement was on "massive life support" and had just a "1% chance of living" after he rejected Tehran's latest counterproposal for failing to address its nuclear program.[1][2]

Speaking alongside Dr. Mehmet Oz at an unrelated White House maternal health event, Trump called the Iranian proposal a "piece of garbage" and said he had not even finished reading it. "I would call it the weakest right now after reading that piece of garbage they sent us," he said during an Oval Office appearance.[2]

items.title: Iran calls its peace terms 'generous' after Trump rejection

featured_image.name: Iran says US making ‘unreasonable’ demands in negotiations to end war

items.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry pushed back Monday against President Donald Trump's rejection of Tehran's latest counterproposal to end the ten-week war, as oil prices surged and prospects for a diplomatic resolution dimmed further.

items.title: Putin says war 'coming to an end' as Germany rejects his peace mediator

featured_image.name: Putin suggests Russia's war on Ukraine 'coming to an end'

items.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin told reporters on Saturday that he believes the war in Ukraine is "approaching its end," hours after presiding over the most diminished Victory Day parade in Moscow in nearly two decades — one that for the first time since 2007 featured no tanks, missiles, or other heavy military equipment on Red Square. The remarks, made on May 9 amid a U.S.-brokered three-day ceasefire, drew immediate skepticism from analysts who said they were aimed at a domestic audience rather than reflecting any genuine shift toward peace.[1][2]

items.title: Second Qatar LNG tanker approaches Hormuz as Pakistan negotiates more shipments

featured_image.name: Qatari LNG Tanker Crosses Strait of Hormuz

items.description: A Qatari tanker carrying liquefied natural gas crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, marking the first successful LNG transit through the chokepoint since the US-Iran war began on February 28, according to ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg. A second vessel, the Mihzem, is now also approaching the strait en route to Pakistan.[1][2]

items.title: Trump calls Iran's response to US peace plan 'totally unacceptable'

featured_image.name: Trump says war will be ‘over quickly’ as Iran reviews US peace proposal

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Sunday rejected Iran's reply to the latest American ceasefire proposal, calling it "totally unacceptable" and casting fresh doubt on prospects for ending a war now in its fourth month. The dismissal came hours after Tehran transmitted its formal response through Pakistani mediators, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA.[1][2]

The exchange marks the latest failure in a series of proposals and counterproposals traded between Washington and Tehran since a fragile ceasefire took effect on April 8. Despite weeks of shuttle diplomacy involving Pakistan, Qatar and other intermediaries, the two sides remain far apart on core issues including Iran's nuclear program, the fate of the Strait of Hormuz and the scope of American sanctions relief.[3]

items.title: Iran threatens 'decisive' response to UK, French warships near Hormuz

featured_image.name: UK Sends HMS Dragon to the Strait of Hormuz

items.description: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi warned on Sunday that any French or British warships entering the Strait of Hormuz to accompany U.S. forces would face a "decisive and immediate response" from Iran's armed forces, escalating a standoff over one of the world's most strategically vital waterways.[1][2][3]
